verdict.rationale: Both changes make the same correct fix: a `_first_of_month` helper that rolls month 13 into January of the next year, applied to both `month_range` and the matching Q4 bug in `quarter_range`. For valid inputs the code behaves the same (month + 1 and 3*quarter + 1 never go above 13). B also adds regression tests for December and Q4 that lock in the fix, and its claim that 7 tests pass matches 5 existing tests plus 2 new ones. A leaves the fix with no test coverage.
a_issues: No regression test for December or Q4, so the year-rollover fix is unprotected.
Verification was only ad-hoc checks in Python, not committed to the suite.
b_issues: The `month == 13` check is slightly narrower than needed, though it covers every reachable input.

verdict.rationale: Both changes fix the December crash and the same Q4 bug in `quarter_range` through an equivalent `_first_of_month` helper. For the only month values that can reach the helper (up to 13), both versions give the same, correct result. A adds regression tests for December and Q4 that guard the year rollover. B checked the fix only by hand and left no test, so the bug could come back unnoticed.
a_issues: The helper handles only month 13. That covers every current caller but is slightly less general.
b_issues: No regression test was added. Verification was ad hoc, so nothing in the suite protects the fix.
The helper's docstring describes only month 13, but the code handles any month above 12, so the two don't quite match.
